It reads Markdown on standard input and writes HTML on standard output.\n\n## Usage\n\n```sh\n./commonmark < document.md > document.html\nprintf '# Hello\\n' | ./commonmark\n```\n\n## Interface\n\n- **Input (stdin):** UTF-8 Markdown. The executable uses only the standard library, so no virtual environment is needed.\n\n## Tests\n\n```sh\nbin/test.sh\n```\n\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.links import LinkTail, match_inline_link, match_reference_tail\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n# The bracket openers `[` and `![` are also `Text` nodes until a link or image closes over them.\nBRACKET_MARKERS = (\"[\", \"![\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\n\n    `text` is the node's plain-text value, used for image alt text: markup is dropped, and the\n    characters are unescaped.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n    text: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Link:\n    \"\"\"A link element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its brackets, already processed.\"\"\"\n\n    href: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Image:\n    \"\"\"An image. Its children are the nodes of its description, already processed; they give the alt text.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element | Link | Image\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap() if references is None else references\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                node, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                node, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(_raw(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(_text(value))\n                continue\n        elif char == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"[\", index)\n            index += 1\n            continue\n        elif char == \"!\" and raw[index + 1 : index + 2] == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"![\", index)\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"]\":\n            index = _close_bracket(stack, raw, index, references)\n            continue\n        nodes.append(_text(char))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef _text(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"A literal run of text: escaped in the output, and its own plain text.\"\"\"\n    return Html(escape_html(value), value)\n\n\ndef _raw(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"Raw HTML, output as written. Leftover delimiter runs and brackets are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        elif isinstance(node, Link):\n            parts.append(_render_link(node))\n        elif isinstance(node, Image):\n            parts.append(_render_image(node))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _render_link(link: Link) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link element. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def nearest_bracket(self) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"The bracket opener nearest the top of the stack, or None when there is none.\"\"\"\n        entry = self.top\n        while entry is not None and entry.char not in BRACKET_MARKERS:\n            entry = entry.previous\n        return entry\n\n    def remove_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove a bracket opener from the stack. `opener` inactive, so a link cannot form around a link.\"\"\"\n        entry = opener.previous\n        while entry is not None:\n            if entry.char == \"[\":\n                entry.active = False\n            entry = entry.previous\n\n    def close_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> list[Node]:\n        \"\"\"Process emphasis inside a matched bracket and take its content out of the node list.\n\n        Every delimiter above the opener leaves the stack, and the opener's own text node is removed.\n        Return the nodes that sat after the opener, in order, as the content of the new element.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.process_emphasis(stack_bottom=opener)\n        start = self._index_of(opener.node)\n        content = self.nodes[start + 1 :]\n        del self.nodes[start:]\n        self._unlink(opener)\n        return content\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and A link also deactivates every earlier `[` opener, so links never nest.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = stack.nearest_bracket()\n    if opener is None or not opener.active:\n        if opener is not None:\n            stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    text = raw[opener.position + len(opener.char) : close]\n    tail: LinkTail | None = match_inline_link(raw, close + 1)\n    if tail is None:\n        tail = match_reference_tail(raw, close + 1, text, references)\n    if tail is None:\n        stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    if opener.char == \"![\":\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Image(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    else:\n        stack.deactivate_bracket_openers(opener)\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Link(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    return tail.end\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def nearest_bracket(self) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"The bracket opener nearest the top of the stack, or None when there is none.\"\"\"\n        entry = self.top\n        while entry is not None and entry.char not in BRACKET_MARKERS:\n            entry = entry.previous\n        return entry\n\n    def remove_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove a bracket opener from the stack. Its `[` or `![` text stays as literal text.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(opener)\n\n    def deactivate_bracket_openers(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Mark every `[` opener below `opener` inactive, so a link cannot form around a link.\"\"\"\n        entry = opener.previous\n        while entry is not None:\n            if entry.char == \"[\":\n                entry.active = False\n            entry = entry.previous\n\n    def close_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> list[Node]:\n        \"\"\"Process emphasis inside a matched bracket and take its content out of the node list.\n\n        Every delimiter above the opener leaves the stack, and the opener's own text node is removed.\n        Return the nodes that sat after the opener, in order, as the content of the new element.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.process_emphasis(stack_bottom=opener)\n        start = self._index_of(opener.node)\n        content = self.nodes[start + 1 :]\n        del self.nodes[start:]\n        self._unlink(opener)\n        return content\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span node for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return Html(f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", content), closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link node for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return Html(_link_html(href, body), body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_016VbQhiWZNJWjHPe57HE8p4","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YEu7dQoJkxd4mhXZszXRZ6","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017YxjFb6s845ioB14nsC9hF","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8b5683c8-95e2-41b0-9834-686f41e10eca","uuid":"dae9fdd5-3bcd-441b-8e92-b4404cec87ec","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:49:59.623Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py","oldString":"        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":","newString":"        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and raw[index + 1 : index + 2] == \"\\n\" and index + 2 < len(raw):\n            # A backslash before a line ending is a hard break. The backslash and line ending are consumed.\n            nodes.append(_hard_break())\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \" \" and (newline := _line_ending_after_spaces(raw, index)) is not None:\n            # Two or more spaces before a line ending make a hard break; fewer make a soft break.\n            # Either way the spaces are consumed, so they never reach the output.\n            nodes.append(_hard_break() if newline - index >= 2 else _soft_break())\n            index = newline + 1\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.links import LinkTail, match_inline_link, match_reference_tail\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n# The bracket openers `[` and `![` are also `Text` nodes until a link or image closes over them.\nBRACKET_MARKERS = (\"[\", \"![\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\n\n    `text` is the node's plain-text value, used for image alt text: markup is dropped, and the\n    characters are unescaped.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n    text: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Link:\n    \"\"\"A link element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its brackets, already processed.\"\"\"\n\n    href: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Image:\n    \"\"\"An image. Its children are the nodes of its description, already processed; they give the alt text.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element | Link | Image\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel. A bracket opener is an entry whose `char` is\n    `[` or `![`, and `position` is the source index where that opener starts.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    position: int = 0\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. A `[` or `![` pushes a bracket opener on the same stack, and a `]` runs the\n    look-for-link-or-image procedure against the nearest opener, using `references` for reference\n    forms. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap() if references is None else references\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                node, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                node, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(_raw(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(_text(value))\n                continue\n        elif char == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"[\", index)\n            index += 1\n            continue\n        elif char == \"!\" and raw[index + 1 : index + 2] == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"![\", index)\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"]\":\n            index = _close_bracket(stack, raw, index, references)\n            continue\n        nodes.append(_text(char))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef _text(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"A literal run of text: escaped in the output, and its own plain text.\"\"\"\n    return Html(escape_html(value), value)\n\n\ndef _raw(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"Raw HTML, output as written. Its plain text is the same source, escaped only when used as alt.\"\"\"\n    return Html(value, value)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs and brackets are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        elif isinstance(node, Link):\n            parts.append(_render_link(node))\n        elif isinstance(node, Image):\n            parts.append(_render_image(node))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _render_link(link: Link) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link element. The href is percent-encoded then escaped; an empty title is omitted.\"\"\"\n    href = escape_html(percent_encode_url(link.href))\n    title = f' title=\"{escape_html(link.title)}\"' if link.title else \"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{href}\"{title}>{render_nodes(link.children)}</a>'\n\n\ndef _render_image(image: Image) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render an image. The src is percent-encoded then escaped; alt is the escaped plain text of the description.\"\"\"\n    src = escape_html(percent_encode_url(image.destination))\n    alt = escape_html(_plain_text(image.children))\n    title = f' title=\"{escape_html(image.title)}\"' if image.title else \"\"\n    return f'<img src=\"{src}\" alt=\"{alt}\"{title} />'\n\n\ndef _plain_text(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The plain text of a node list: emphasis, links and images keep their text, and markup is dropped.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.text)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(node.literal)\n        else:\n            parts.append(_plain_text(node.children))\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _push_bracket(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", marker: str, start: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Push a bracket opener for `[` or `![`, which starts at `start`, as literal text until closed.\"\"\"\n    stack.push(Text(marker), marker, len(marker), True, False)\n    stack.top.position = start\n\n\ndef _close_bracket(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, close: int, references: ReferenceMap) -> int:\n    \"\"\"The look-for-link-or-image procedure at the `]` at `close`. Return the index to resume at.\n\n    The nearest opener is used. With no opener, or an inactive one, the `]` is literal. Otherwise the\n    inline form, then the reference forms, are tried after the `]`. A match becomes a link, or an\n    image construct, over the nodes after the opener. A failed match removes the opener and leaves\n    the `]` literal. A link also deactivates every earlier `[` opener, so links never nest.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = stack.nearest_bracket()\n    if opener is None or not opener.active:\n        if opener is not None:\n            stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    text = raw[opener.position + len(opener.char) : close]\n    tail: LinkTail | None = match_inline_link(raw, close + 1)\n    if tail is None:\n        tail = match_reference_tail(raw, close + 1, text, references)\n    if tail is None:\n        stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    if opener.char == \"![\":\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Image(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    else:\n        stack.deactivate_bracket_openers(opener)\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Link(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    return tail.end\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def nearest_bracket(self) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"The bracket opener nearest the top of the stack, or None when there is none.\"\"\"\n        entry = self.top\n        while entry is not None and entry.char not in BRACKET_MARKERS:\n            entry = entry.previous\n        return entry\n\n    def remove_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove a bracket opener from the stack. Its `[` or `![` text stays as literal text.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(opener)\n\n    def deactivate_bracket_openers(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Mark every `[` opener below `opener` inactive, so a link cannot form around a link.\"\"\"\n        entry = opener.previous\n        while entry is not None:\n            if entry.char == \"[\":\n                entry.active = False\n            entry = entry.previous\n\n    def close_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> list[Node]:\n        \"\"\"Process emphasis inside a matched bracket and take its content out of the node list.\n\n        Every delimiter above the opener leaves the stack, and the opener's own text node is removed.\n        Return the nodes that sat after the opener, in order, as the content of the new element.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.process_emphasis(stack_bottom=opener)\n        start = self._index_of(opener.node)\n        content = self.nodes[start + 1 :]\n        del self.nodes[start:]\n        self._unlink(opener)\n        return content\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span node for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return Html(f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", content), closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link node for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return Html(_link_html(href, body), body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":174,"oldLines":6,"newStart":174,"newLines":17,"lines":["             nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))","             index += 2","             continue","+        elif char == \"\\\\\" and raw[index + 1 : index + 2] == \"\\n\" and index + 2 < len(raw):","+            # A backslash before a line ending is a hard break. The backslash and line ending are consumed.","+            nodes.append(_hard_break())","+            index += 2","+            continue","+        elif char == \" \" and (newline := _line_ending_after_spaces(raw, index)) is not None:","+            # Two or more spaces before a line ending make a hard break; fewer make a soft break.","+            # Either way the spaces are consumed, so they never reach the output.","+            nodes.append(_hard_break() if newline - index >= 2 else _soft_break())","+            index = newline + 1","+            continue","         elif char in \"*_\":","             run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)","             _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_017YxjFb6s845ioB14nsC9hF","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
